newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia-Japan iron ore talks begin Monday.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia-Japan iron ore talks begin Monday.

text.p: Australian iron ore producers will begin negotiating with Japanese steel mills in Tokyo next week over price and tonnage terms for the 1997/98 Japanese fiscal year, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) said.

First meetings between Australian suppliers and Japanese buyers would involve a preliminary exchange of views on the market and would be held on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday next week, a BHP spokeswoman said.
Formal meetings would begin in mid-December, she said.
Key iron ore markets had been of concern until recently, but encouraging signs were emerging from Europe of a strengthening position, she said.
Commitments by the Japanese government to stimulate the economy and strengthening imports by China produced a more positive picture and concern was dissipating, she said.
"In all we are confident about a reasonable price outcome," she said.
But she would not comment on whether Australian producers would be seeking a price rise for shipments in the coming Japanese fiscal year, which begins April 1.
BHP won a 5.00 to 6.00 percent price rise for Australian shipments to Japan in 1996/97.
The RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd-owned Hamersley Iron Pty Ltd, Australia's other major iron ore producer, won a 6.0 percent price rise for iron ore fines and a 5.0 percent increase for lump ore.
North Ltd's unit Robe River iron won a 7.4 percent price rise for fines.

Australian iron ore exports, with Japan the dominant customer, have been forecast to rise by seven million tonnes to 133.5 million tonnes valued at A$3.1 billion in Australian fiscal 1996/97 ending June 30.
